summary: Build supplier risk, continuity, and recovery planning skills through practical supply chain exercises. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Supply chain resilience planning helps procurement, logistics, and operations professionals map critical dependencies and prepare responses to disruption. The course covers risk registers, supplier tiering and flow mapping, business impact analysis, contingency design, recovery priorities, and escalation workflows, drawing on ISO 31000 risk concepts and ISO 22301 continuity planning. Participants also practise creating a spreadsheet dashboard to monitor supply risk indicators and report resilience actions, ownership, and trade-offs.
audienceIntro: This foundation course is designed for professionals who map, assess, coordinate, or report supply chain disruption risks in day-to-day operations. This course is designed for: Supply chain planners coordinating demand, supply, and recovery priorities. Procurement specialists assessing critical supplier dependencies and sourcing alternatives. Supplier risk analysts maintaining supply disruption registers and exposure assessments. Logistics coordinators evaluating route, carrier, port, and capacity constraints. Business continuity officers linking supply interruptions to continuity plans. Supply chain managers prioritizing resilience actions across operating teams. Inventory planners setting buffer and replenishment responses for critical materials. Operations risk specialists assessing production dependencies and recovery requirements. Sourcing managers preparing contingency options for constrained supplier categories. Supply chain executives reporting disruption readiness, recovery priorities, and investment needs.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Basic familiarity with procurement, logistics, supply planning, or operations is useful. No coding is required. Bring access to spreadsheet software for the dashboard exercise; no specialized supply chain platform is required.
